passage: The pressure cooker hissed in the kitchen of their Kolkata flat as Sarika sat down across from her daughter. Irawati braced for shouting. It didn't come. "I'm hurt that you lied about the fair," Sarika said, "and I also want to understand why you felt you couldn't just ask me." Irawati stared at the tablecloth. "Because you'd have said no. You always say no to anything after dark." Sarika was quiet. "Do I?" "Every time, Ma." Sarika opened her mouth, then closed it. "I didn't know it felt like that." Irawati looked up, surprised. She had expected a lecture, not this. "I didn't think you'd even want to know why," she said.

qa.q: What did Irawati lie about?
qa.a: She lied about the fair.

qa.q: What had Irawati expected from her mother?
qa.a: She expected shouting or a lecture, and was surprised when her mother asked why instead.

qa.q: Why was Sarika's opening line a good turning point?
qa.a: It named her hurt honestly while also asking for Irawati's reason, which made it safe for Irawati to tell the truth.

qa.q: What did Sarika hear that she didn't expect?
qa.a: She heard that she always says no to anything after dark, which she hadn't realised felt that way to Irawati.

grounding: Shows a mother naming her hurt while asking why her daughter felt unable to ask, and the teen admitting she feared a refusal.

passage:
"Sit, Gautam. I'm not going to shout."
"That's what you said last time."
"Fair." Jaya took a breath and looked at her son. "I'm hurt that you lied about the cricket camp. Really hurt. And I also want to know why you felt you couldn't ask me."
Gautam picked at the sofa cushion. "Because you'd say no."
"You don't know that."
"Ma, you said no to the school trip. And the concert. And Dev's birthday. I stopped asking."
Jaya was silent for a long moment. "I didn't realise I'd said no that many times."
"I didn't think you'd ever admit that," Gautam said quietly.
"And I didn't know you were scared of asking me. I thought you just didn't care about the rules."
They looked at each other, both a little surprised.

qa.q: What did Gautam lie about?
qa.a: He lied about the cricket camp.

qa.q: What had Jaya believed about Gautam before this talk?
qa.a: She thought he simply didn't care about the rules, not that he was scared of asking her.

qa.q: What made this conversation work where "last time" didn't?
qa.a: Jaya stayed calm, named her hurt, and asked why, which let Gautam explain instead of defend.

qa.q: What surprised Gautam about his mother?
qa.a: He didn't expect her to admit she'd said no so many times, which suggests she was really listening.

grounding: Shows a mother voicing her hurt and asking why her teen couldn't ask her, and both hearing something they did not expect.

passage:
I thought Mummy would shout. Instead, after dinner, she sat on the edge of my bed.
"I'm hurt that you lied about going to Amandeep's party," she said. "And I also want to know why you felt you couldn't ask me."
I stared at the ceiling. Then it just came out. "Because I was scared you'd say no. You always say no, and then you look so disappointed in me."
Mummy was quiet. "I didn't know you saw it like that," she said. "I say no because I get scared. I didn't know you were scared too."
We both sat there, surprised. I'm Jasleen, and that was the first time I felt like she heard me.

qa.q: Whose party did Jasleen lie about?
qa.a: Amandeep's party.

qa.q: What was Jasleen feeling when admitting the reason for the lie?
qa.a: Jasleen was scared of being refused and of Mummy's disappointment, and then surprised and relieved at being heard.

qa.q: Why did Mummy's approach help?
qa.a: She named her hurt but also asked why Jasleen couldn't ask her, which let Jasleen admit the fear and both learn something unexpected.

qa.q: What was Mummy experiencing when Jasleen explained?
qa.a: She was surprised to learn that Jasleen saw her that way, and she admitted her own fear behind the no's.

grounding: A mother tells her teen she is hurt by the lie and wants to know why the teen couldn't ask, and both hear something they did not expect.

passage:
School counsellor's note, Tuesday

Today I met Vinita and her daughter Madhuri, after Madhuri lied about a weekend trip.
Vinita started by saying, "I'm hurt by the lie. And I also want to understand why you felt you couldn't ask me."
Madhuri was silent for a long time. Then she said, "Because I thought you'd say no, and then be angry for days."
Vinita looked shocked. "I didn't know you were afraid of me."
"Not afraid. Just… scared of the no."
They both went quiet. I asked each of them to say one thing they had just learned. Vinita said, "That my no's feel so final." Madhuri said, "That Mummy was hurt, not just angry."
We'll meet again next week.

qa.q: What did Madhuri lie about?
qa.a: A weekend trip.

qa.q: What was Madhuri feeling when she explained why she lied?
qa.a: She was scared of her mother's no and of the anger that followed.

qa.q: What made this conversation work?
qa.a: Vinita named her hurt but also asked why Madhuri couldn't ask, which let Madhuri admit her fear, and the counsellor helped both say what they had learned.

qa.q: What was Vinita experiencing when she heard Madhuri's reason?
qa.a: She was shocked, realising that her no's felt so final to her daughter.

grounding: A counsellor records a mother naming her hurt and asking why her daughter couldn't ask, and both learn something unexpected.

passage:
Sunday, late

Mumma found out about me and Siddharth going to the movie on Friday, when I'd said I was at Priyanka's.
I waited all day for the explosion. It didn't come.
At dinner, she said, "I'm hurt you lied. And I also want to know why you felt you couldn't just ask me."
I almost cried. I said, "Because I was scared you'd say no and then be disappointed in me for even asking."
Mumma put down her spoon. "I didn't know that. I thought you just didn't want to tell me things."
We talked for an hour. She told me she's scared of the city at night. I told her I'm scared of her silence.
I didn't expect any of that. — Ankita

qa.q: Where did Ankita say she was on Friday?
qa.a: At Priyanka's.

qa.q: What was Ankita feeling as she waited all day?
qa.a: Ankita felt anxious, waiting for an explosion, and then almost cried with relief when her mother asked calmly.

qa.q: What made the conversation turn into an honest one?
qa.a: Mumma named her hurt but also asked why Ankita couldn't ask, which allowed Ankita to admit her fear and both to share things they didn't know.

qa.q: What was Mumma experiencing when Ankita explained?
qa.a: She was surprised and moved, having thought Ankita just didn't want to share, and she opened up about her own fear of the city at night.

grounding: A mother names her hurt and asks why her teen couldn't ask; the teen admits fear of refusal, and both hear something unexpected.
